items.title: Gaza plans to invest 126 million US dollar in photovoltaic power plant
items.summary: Maputo, 21 Oct (AIM) – The Mozambican government plans to invest about 126 million US dollars in a photovoltaic power plant to supply electricity to mining companies in the southern province of Gaza. According to the governor of Gaza Province, Alfeu Cuna, who was speaking on at the Conference on Adding Value to Mineral Resources (CAVAME-d 2026), which is taking place in the port city of Nacala, in the northern province of Nampula, the plant is expected to strengthen electricity supplies to mining companies operating in the province, creating conditions for the development of industries linked to mineral extraction. The governor highlighted existing electricity infrastructure, including the Lionde and Xai-Xai substations and power transmission lines, which could support the expansion of industrial activities. He also pointed to the importance of reliable electricity supplies for establishing mineral processing facilities in Mabalane and Mapai, two districts in Gaza province where limestone deposits have been identified.

items.title: SACBM and SAPCC sign landmark partnership to strengthen business cooperation between South Africa and Mozambique
items.summary: Founded in 2013, the SAPCC is a member-driven, non-profit organisation representing more than 2,000 members across Southern Africa. It is recognised by both Portuguese and South African authorities and plays an important role in fostering business relationships and promoting commercial opportunities SACBM represented at the SAPCC Gala 2026 SACBM was honoured to attend the SAPCC Cell C Business Excellence Awards 2026, represented by its Chairman, Filipe Raposo, and CEO, Dra Sonia Chembeze The prestigious gala brought together approximately 500 guests for an evening celebrating business excellence, leadership, entrepreneurship, Portuguese culture and the strength of the regional business community A major highlight of the day was the signing of the MOU between SACBM and SAPCC.

items.title: Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger 'good idea' as companies explore union
items.summary: Musk confirmed the long standing speculation of a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX but warned that it would be premature to assume it is happening for sure Tech billionaire Elon Musk on Tursday said a merger between his two companies, SpaceX and Tesla, would be a "good idea" and that they had formed special committees to discuss the matter — confirming speculation of a possibly union "I think it would be a good idea, but it's really up to the special committees of both companies," Musk said "Because ​I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees," which was comprised of independent directors, he told investors on a conference call Shares of the space tech company rose 8% in trade over Musk's comment, while Tesla's shares rose 1.8%.

items.title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
items.summary: Nearly 5,000 healthcare workers have been trained to deal with Ebola Kenya is grappling with its first ever outbreak of Ebola, a disease which neighbouring countries, such as Uganda and Democratic Republic of Congo, are used to dealing with Nine cases have now been confirmed including its first patient, who travelled from DR Congo and died two weeks ago Four relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner have now tested positive, meaning they are all linked to him But concerns are rising that the virus could start spreading further, even as the government has sought to assure citizens The US has warned it citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert Kenyans have been expressing their concerns that the disease could spread more widely More than 4,000 people have died since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according…

items.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
items.summary: Ameth Bek Hospital in Abyei town has been treating people wounded in Monday's attack on the market Sudan's army has been accused of launching several drone strikes that have reportedly killed more than 300 people, including dozens travelling to a funeral The death toll from strikes in two areas of West Kordofan state on Sunday evening was 150, sources told the Sudan War Observatory, which tracks the conflict that erupted in 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) In Abyei, a disputed border area between Sudan and South Sudan, 153 people were killed when drones hit a market on Monday, the region's information minister said A military source told the BBC the army had carried out the Abyei attack, saying the market was a fuel supply site for the RSF The attack has raised tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, which jointly administer Abyei, as they both claim ownership to the oil-rich region in a dispute that has remained unresolved since South Sudan ceded in 2011 South Sudan has summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest.
